columns.label: Locate Evidence
columns.description: Freeze definitions, corpus access, and source identifiers before cleaning.

columns.label: Audit Data
columns.description: Run corpus-first detectors and source-level quarantine before retraining.

columns.label: Decide Retraining
columns.description: Gate any model training on a frozen clean manifest and validation report.

columns.label: Evaluate Models
columns.description: Validate the cleaned manifest and keep model probes as acceptance tests.

columns.label: Write/Share
columns.description: Turn evidence, manifests, and residual-risk claims into team-facing outputs.

tasks.title: Freeze cutoff and contamination definitions
tasks.done: A short policy states the exact cutoff rule, allowed/disallowed/borderline text, and separate treatment of pretraining, SFT, tokenizer/vocab, metadata, prefaces, notes, and boilerplate.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo says direct cleaning must start by defining what counts as contamination for <=1929 or <1930.
tasks.notes: This should settle revised editions, modern introductions, OCR headers, and whether separable paratext can be stripped.

tasks.title: Confirm the contaminated model location
tasks.done: The exact repository or checkpoint is written down, including access status and which model family/cutoff it belongs to.
tasks.evidence: Project X update identified history-llms/ranke-0.6b-1913-1106-cont-1 as the contaminated model.
tasks.notes: Keep this as a reference artifact for calibration, not as the production target.

tasks.title: Document what the contaminated model teaches us
tasks.done: A short, didactic note explains what the contaminated model shows, why it matters, and how it will be used for calibration.
tasks.evidence: Joachim asked for a simple write-up of the contaminated model and what can be learned from it.
tasks.notes: Possible follow-up: put the artifact on Hugging Face once the write-up is clear.

tasks.title: Map all training inputs and corpus locations
tasks.done: A complete inventory identifies pretraining, tokenizer/vocab, SFT/instruction data, caches, prior dropped data, CSCS/ALPS paths, and who can access each item.
tasks.evidence: Joachim asked Daniel/Dominik to locate the data; the Pro memo says no certification is possible without exact corpus paths and training inputs.
tasks.notes: This now includes tokenizer and SFT inputs, not just the pretraining text.

tasks.title: Build raw source inventory and stable IDs
tasks.done: raw_source_inventory.parquet or equivalent exists with document_id, source_id, source_family_id, raw path, dataset/source metadata, publication/edition years, token counts, and hashes.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo says source-level decontamination is impossible without stable document/source/family IDs.
tasks.notes: This is the key prerequisite for all scalable detector outputs and source-level quarantine.

tasks.title: Create normalized text index with offsets
tasks.done: A normalized document index supports lowercase/Unicode/OCR-hyphen/whitespace-normalized scans while preserving offsets back to raw text and chunk boundaries.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo recommends normalized text for scanning but raw offsets for evidence snippets and audit.
tasks.notes: Keep high-churn working files off Dropbox if this runs at corpus scale.

tasks.title: Run disambiguated hard-marker scan for suspicious domains
tasks.done: A full-corpus marker pass writes detector_hits.jsonl with document_id, source_id, source_family_id, marker, bucket, evidence span, confidence, and action hint.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo recommends expanding find_contamination.py into a production detector for US politics, Vietnam, Cold War, WWII, civil rights, postwar institutions, and science.
tasks.notes: Use disambiguating context windows for ambiguous names such as Kennedy, Normandy, Israel, Nagasaki, and Reagan.

tasks.title: Run metadata, edition, and boilerplate scan
tasks.done: metadata_conflicts.parquet or equivalent flags post-cutoff publication/edition years, revised editions, modern introductions, scan headers, OCR boilerplate, ISBNs, upload dates, and modern file names.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo identifies metadata/edition/reprint checks as one of the highest-value detectors.
tasks.notes: Decide whether modern paratext can be stripped or whether the whole edition/source should be quarantined.

tasks.title: Compare dropped Xmas data against random corpus samples
tasks.done: A ranked term/source list compares dropped Xmas material against random kept corpus samples and converts over-represented terms into scanner seeds.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo names prior dropped data as a dirty-reference source and search-seed source.
tasks.notes: Feed both marker expansion and near-duplicate dirty-reference construction.

tasks.title: Build dirty-reference near-duplicate index
tasks.done: A dirty-reference library and MinHash/SimHash-style matching identify modern/post-cutoff paragraphs, source mirrors, boilerplate, SFT content, and prior dropped material embedded in the corpus.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo recommends near-duplicate matching to catch formal modern histories and copied post-cutoff reference text that keyword search misses.
tasks.notes: Reference sources should include dropped Xmas data, modern history/biography sources, boilerplate, and known contaminated slices.

tasks.title: Train and score temporal-writing classifiers
tasks.done: Genre-balanced fastText and character n-gram classifiers are trained for relevant cutoffs, evaluated by genre/topic/leave-topic-out tests, and used to score corpus passages and sources.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo upgrades the existing fastText idea into a 1929/1930 date-of-writing detector stack.
tasks.notes: Avoid learning topic instead of date; include formal post-cutoff histories, not only modern web text.

tasks.title: Audit SFT and tokenizer/vocab inputs separately
tasks.done: sft_clean_manifest.jsonl and tokenizer_vocab_audit.md separately report or quarantine post-cutoff instruction examples, assistant facts, benchmark artifacts, tokenizer training text, modern tokens, and template contamination.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo warns that SFT or tokenizer contamination can mimic or explain model contamination even when pretraining is clean.
tasks.notes: Keep base-pretraining, instruct/SFT, and tokenizer claims separate.

tasks.title: Aggregate detector outputs into source risk ledger
tasks.done: source_risk_ledger.parquet combines marker hits, temporal scores, near-duplicate hits, metadata conflicts, boilerplate scores, audit status, token weights, and recommended action by source/source family.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo says the key removal decision should usually be source family, source/edition, or document, not isolated sentence.
tasks.notes: This task also depends in practice on metadata, temporal-classifier, and near-duplicate outputs.

tasks.title: Apply source-level quarantine policy
tasks.done: quarantine_manifest.jsonl records every excluded document/source/family with reason codes such as POST_CUTOFF_EVENT_MARKER, POST_CUTOFF_METADATA, SOURCE_FAMILY_CONTAMINATED, SFT_POST_CUTOFF, or TOKENIZER_VOCAB_POST_CUTOFF.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo recommends aggressive high-recall quarantine before final keep decisions, with stable reason codes rather than silent deletion.
tasks.notes: Use source/family drops for repeated or unstrippable contamination; passage stripping only for deterministic boilerplate.

tasks.title: Freeze clean training manifest
tasks.done: clean_training_manifest.jsonl is versioned and includes only approved documents/sources after detector runs, source-level quarantine, SFT/tokenizer separation, seeded validation, and audit review.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo says training should read a manifest, not an ad hoc cleaned folder.
tasks.notes: This is the artifact that gates 1.7B or any large clean run.

tasks.title: Freeze validation and audit protocol
tasks.done: A validation protocol fixes risk strata, audit labels, sample sizes, token-weighting rules, seeded-injection tests, historical cutoff simulations, and residual-risk reporting before final results are inspected.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo recommends strategic audit and validation without full LLM training.
tasks.notes: Use evidence grades such as hard contamination, soft suspicion, false positive, modern boilerplate, and metadata error.

tasks.title: Run token-weighted stratified manual audit
tasks.done: Audit labels cover hard hits, soft hits, high temporal scores, metadata conflicts, near-duplicates, boilerplate, high-token source families, random kept documents, and random quarantine documents; residual contamination upper bounds are estimated.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo says zero hits in a sample is only an upper bound, not proof of clean data.
tasks.notes: Use two labels and adjudication for borderline cases if feasible.

tasks.title: Run seeded-injection and historical cutoff validation
tasks.done: A report measures document-level, source-level, and token-weighted recall/precision for injected post-cutoff documents, modern prefaces, embedded paragraphs, ambiguous entities, OCR corruption, and simulated earlier cutoffs.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo says validation can happen without full model training by injecting known dirty material and simulating cutoffs like 1900 or 1913.
tasks.notes: Target near-perfect source-level recall for explicit seeded contamination in suspicious domains.

tasks.title: Freeze post-cleaning acceptance battery
tasks.done: A locked acceptance battery states domains, item counts, screening rules, metrics, and decision thresholds before any post-cleaning model is scored.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo keeps probes as final acceptance tests, not the primary corpus detector.
tasks.notes: Existing exploratory batteries remain search-seed sources and method-development artifacts.

tasks.title: Set residual-risk and acceptance thresholds
tasks.done: The team defines acceptable source-level recall, audit upper bounds, broad/narrow acceptance-test thresholds, and conservative wording for residual contamination.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo recommends claims like below detectable threshold, with confidence bounds, instead of clean.
tasks.notes: Include document-level, token-weighted, source-family, SFT, and tokenizer/vocab risk.

tasks.title: Confirm Talkie logprob access on WestAI
tasks.done: The Talkie base model can be scored with prompt-continuation sum log-probabilities on suitable GPU hardware.
tasks.evidence: Private messages noted Talkie should use the base model on WestAI GPU, with logprob access needed for the same metric.
tasks.notes: Lower priority than corpus-first cleaning; keep as an acceptance-test capability.

tasks.title: Gate the 1.7B diagnostic decision on clean-manifest validation
tasks.done: A go/no-go memo states whether 1.7B is needed after corpus validation, what locked acceptance battery it answers, expected cost, and what result would block the large run.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo says to skip 1.7B until the corpus inventory, detector stack, source quarantine, clean manifest, seeded-injection recall, SFT/tokenizer scans, and acceptance probes are frozen.
tasks.notes: Do not run 1.7B as an anxiety-driven cleaning loop; use it only as a post-manifest gate.

tasks.title: Train the 1.7B calibration model if greenlit
tasks.done: If greenlit, a 1.7B model is trained on the exact frozen clean manifest, tokenizer, and preprocessing pipeline and scored once on the locked acceptance battery.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo allows 1.7B only after manifest freeze and validation, as a gate before the large clean run.
tasks.notes: If it fails on a domain, return to corpus/source search for that domain rather than redesigning probes.

tasks.title: Decide whether to skip 1.7B and train one large clean model
tasks.done: A go/no-go decision chooses between no training yet, a 1.7B gate, or one large clean model from scratch, based on manifest validation and locked acceptance tests.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo says the default should be corpus-first cleaning, then train once; 1.7B is optional only after validation.
tasks.notes: If model acceptance fails, return to source search for the fired domain rather than restarting the probe design loop.

tasks.title: Collect WVS model-survey evidence
tasks.done: A short note summarizes evidence that modern models can approximate survey responses well enough for the WVS application.
tasks.evidence: Private chat asked Guohui to look into proof that modern models are close to surveys.
tasks.notes: Keep separate from the contamination audit, but link it to the application narrative.

tasks.title: Write validation report and residual-risk claim
tasks.done: A team-facing report states detector recall, audit precision, residual upper bounds, what was quarantined, what remains uncertain, and conservative wording such as below detectable threshold.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo emphasizes honest residual-risk language and source-level evidence before training.
tasks.notes: This should accompany the clean manifest and go/no-go decision.

tasks.title: Keep the team aligned on the flow
tasks.done: The team agrees that corpus-first decontamination is the default path, model probes are search seeds or acceptance tests, and the 1.7B run is conditional on manifest validation.
tasks.evidence: The Pro memo reorganizes the work around corpus ledger, detector stack, source-level quarantine, validation, then training gate.
tasks.notes: This dashboard now reflects that operating model.
